situation.person: First-time mother and father of a 0–16-week-old baby in the first 12 weeks postpartum, whose newborn sleeps only on the chest and who have not slept more than 90 minutes at a stretch since discharge
situation.specific_situation: The baby sleeps only on the chest and wakes the moment she is lowered. Nights run in 90-minute fragments with no agreed settle routine, so every night is improvised at 3am. Day and night are flipped, because the baby is wakeful from 1am to 5am while the parents cannot rest by day and no omugwo help exists.
situation.trigger: Discharge home with a newborn whose sleep biology nobody explained; the first night the baby will not settle except on the chest.
situation.problem: No independent sleep stretch and no safe rest plan exist, so the parents doze unsafely on the sofa because no other rest is available.
situation.failed_attempt: Tried the bouncer, swaddling, keeping the baby up, dark rooms, dream feeds and formula top-ups, and read contradictory advice across nine videos, so nothing stuck.
constraints: cannot rest by day and no omugwo help exists

AAP 2022 safe-sleep policy: back-to-sleep every sleep; firm, flat, noninclined surface; room-sharing without bed-sharing ideally for the first 6 months; never fall asleep on a sofa or armchair with an infant.
evidence.source: AAP safe sleep policy statement + technical report 2022 (doi:10.1542/peds.2022-057991)

evidence.claim: WHO postnatal guideline 2022: place the baby supine during the first year; listed newborn danger signs (not feeding well, convulsions, fast breathing, fever, hypothermia, early or prolonged jaundice) require care-seeking.
evidence.source: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience 2022

evidence.claim: NHS newborn guidance teaches day/night cues behaviourally (light, noise, routine at night) and states short fragmented newborn sleep is normal; it does not prescribe sleep-training outcomes.
evidence.source: NHS newborn sleep and safe sleep guidance (accessed 2026-09-17)

evidence.claim: Parent-invented shift splits plus a written rest roster directly prevent the highest-risk outcome in this situation, unintentional sofa or armchair sleep.
evidence.source: Authoring Wave 1 evidence review (community shift practice + AAP harm ranking)

safety.scope_boundary: This transformation coordinates SLEEP A. Newborn sleep survival - settling, day-night rhythm and safe rest only. It does not diagnose, treat, or replace professional care, and it does not cover adjacent situations outside its recorded nucleus.
escalation_rules: Route per the verified shared crisis/escalation list (RED = emergency now, AMBER = urgent today, GREEN = supported this week) - safety-standard 3; no numbers are invented here
